comment: TOML-REFERENCE-ANCHORS. Three facts, and each one is a regression that a spelling-comparing differential cannot catch on its own. (1) THE SOURCE OF A `references` EDGE MUST BE A PUBLISHED SYMBOL. The edge used to be spelled `libraries.<lib>.version.ref`, which no symbol ever carries: an inline table's keys are recorded as `inlineKeys` METADATA on the owning key, not as symbols. Measured over the corpus, 167 of 167 edges bound to ZERO source symbols against 167 of 167 binding targets — unreachable by every incoming query, because `traceCallers` JOINs `brain_symbol` on the source. The oracle spelled the same phantom, so both sides agreed and the lane read 100% covered. The anchor is the owning key; the specificity the phantom carried now travels in `metadata.aliasKeyPath`. (2) A COMMENT IS A NAMED CHILD OF ITS PAIR, so 'the last named child' is the comment and not the value. That made a commented key invisible to scalar detection and dropped its alias with it — 4 of the corpus's 167 aliases sit on a commented line, and the oracle carried the same defect independently until the differential reported it as UNEXPLAINED. (3) An alias naming a final segment declared TWICE emits NO edge: there is no single right answer, and a guess cannot be falsified downstream. The same holds for an alias naming nothing the document declares, which is a string and not a reference.

expectSymbols.name: reference-anchors
expectSymbols.comment: the FILE is the module, named from its stem

expectSymbols.name: libraries.groovy-bom
expectSymbols.comment: the OWNING KEY is the edge's source, and it is a published symbol

expectSymbols.name: versions#2
expectSymbols.comment: the SECOND `[versions]` header collides with the first and takes the deterministic suffix the file's name space already uses

expectSymbols.name: versions#2.detekt
expectSymbols.comment: a COMMENTED key is still a key: `detekt = "1.23.8" # ...` declares this

expectSymbols.name: versions#3
expectSymbols.comment: the THIRD `[versions]` header. A document may repeat a header, and each repeat is its own node rather than a merge into the first.

expectSymbols.name: versions#3.dup
expectSymbols.comment: the FIRST declaration of final segment `dup`

expectSymbols.name: other.dup
expectSymbols.comment: the SECOND declaration of final segment `dup`, which is what makes that alias ambiguous

expectSymbols.name: libraries#2.ambiguous
expectSymbols.comment: declares a `version.ref` alias, and emits NO edge for it

expectSymbols.name: libraries#3.dangling
expectSymbols.comment: declares a `version.ref` alias naming nothing this document declares, and emits NO edge for it

forbidSymbols.name: libraries.groovy-bom.version.ref
forbidSymbols.comment: the PHANTOM source name. No symbol is ever published for a key inside an inline table, so an edge anchored here is unreachable by every incoming query.

forbidSymbols.name: versions.absent
forbidSymbols.comment: an alias naming nothing the document declares is a string, not a reference

expectRelationships.comment: the alias and its target both sit on COMMENTED lines. A comment is a named child, so picking the pair's last named child as its value loses this edge entirely.

forbidRelationships.comment: THE REGRESSION THIS FIXTURE EXISTS FOR: the phantom source spelling. Both endpoints look right to a spelling comparison, so restoring it would leave every other gate green while making the edge unreachable by `traceCallers`.
`dup` is declared twice — `versions#3.dup` and `other.dup` — so there is no single right target and the lane declines rather than guess.
the alias names nothing the document declares, so there is no edge to emit.
